expectations.text: Describes the corrective sequence correctly: nonconformities lead to a corrective action plan assessed by the audit provider (corrective action plan assessment), followed by follow-up assessment(s) verifying implementation
expectations.evidence: "You submit a corrective action plan (CAP) ... The auditor/provider reviews the CAP to confirm the proposed actions would actually close the gap ... You provide evidence of remediation ... back to the audit provider for verification, usually via a remote follow-up review."

expectations.text: States the temporary-label mechanics: temporary labels may be issued on an approved corrective action plan, and they EXPIRE 9 months after the initial assessment's closing meeting
expectations.evidence: Response describes a 'valid with correction requirement' provisional status rather than a temporary label that expires: "the assessment result in the ENX system typically shows as 'valid with correction requirement' (i.e., a provisional/temporary status)". It never states this status/label expires 9 months after the closing meeting; the only mention of 9 months is hedged as "commonly cited in the ENX/TISAX process as up to around 9 months in total ... though the exact deadline depends on the severity of the findings" — not tied to the closing meeting date and not stated as a fixed expiry.

expectations.text: States the hard deadline: all corrective work and follow-up must complete within the 9-month window — miss it and the assessment must be redone
expectations.evidence: Response hedges the consequence instead of stating the fixed rule: "the audit provider can escalate this — potentially resulting in the assessment result being downgraded, marked as not valid, or in a worst case requiring a fresh assessment." It frames a full re-assessment as only one of several possible, severity-dependent outcomes rather than the definite consequence of missing a fixed 9-month window.

expectations.text: Gives substantive remediation guidance for the named areas (access control: e.g., joiner-mover-leaver, privileged access, reviews; supplier management: contracts/security requirements, supplier assessment) tied to reaching target maturity 3 given cutback scoring
expectations.evidence: Section 5 gives good specific remediation detail ("weak joiner/mover/leaver processes", "privileged access", "periodic access reviews", "security clauses in supplier contracts", "supplier risk assessment process") but never ties this back to target maturity 3 or cutback scoring — the word 'cutback' does not appear anywhere in the response, and maturity 3 is mentioned only once in passing in section 1, not connected to the remediation guidance.

expectations.text: Covers the practical mechanics: work with the same audit provider for follow-up, evidence-first remediation (documents + operating records), and final labels (3-year validity) shared via the ENX platform once closed
expectations.evidence: Evidence-first remediation is covered ("updated policies, screenshots/configuration evidence, revised supplier contracts or risk assessments, access reviews performed"), but there is no mention anywhere of the ENX platform or of final labels being valid for 3 years (no occurrence of '3 year', '3-year', or 'ENX platform' in the response).
